title: DECSET 1046 — Push/pop color palette and kitty keyboard
summary: CSI ? 1046 h is reserved/used by some terminals for push/pop color palette (xterm) or enabling the kitty keyboard protocol. CSI ? 1046 l disables it.

frame.note: DEC private modes are CSI sequences with a leading '?' (0x3F) private-parameter prefix. Set = final byte 'h' (DECSET); reset = final byte 'l' (DECRST).

terminator_detail.note: No string terminator: a DEC private mode is a CSI sequence ending at its final byte ('h' to set, 'l' to reset).

params.name: Enable (DECSET)
params.meaning: CSI ? 1046 h Color palette push/pop; kitty keyboard.

gotchas: xterm uses 1046 for push/pop color palette (OSC 4 queries can be saved/restored).
kitty uses a different mechanism (CSI > Ps u) for its keyboard protocol.
Check terminal documentation for the specific meaning.

v1_smoke_test.asserts: DECSET/DECRST 1046 render as byte-exact CSI ? 1046 h/l sequences.
